name: XYZ-Squish
summary: Go-Go with the stretching moved from the arm to the world: the hand stays at its real position and the whole scene is scaled down towards the user, so the hand reaches the points Go-Go would.
howItWorks: As with Z-Squish, the reach mapping is Go-Go's, but the scene is scaled uniformly around the user by the inverse of the mapping, so it shrinks along all axes as the hand extends. A sphere cursor at the rendered hand selects with the controller trigger. In a study with 18 participants it was slower, produced more misclicks and was liked least compared with Go-Go and Z-Squish. In a second study on illusory thresholds, the uniform scaling made the remapping go unnoticed at low distance multipliers, where Go-Go's arm stretch was noticed.
advantages: The remapping can go unnoticed at low multipliers.
The rendered hand stays at its real position.
limitations: Slower and more error-prone than Go-Go in the study.
Scaled targets appear smaller relative to the hand.

relationships.note: Go-Go's distance multiplier is kept unchanged; only what the user sees changes.
Introduced and compared in the same study.
Both scale the world instead of extending the arm.
